label: Triangle Properties
overview: SAT triangle questions test the angle sum rule (all angles sum to 180°), exterior angles, similar triangles, and triangle inequality. Similar triangles are especially common: if two triangles are similar, their corresponding sides are proportional and their corresponding angles are equal. These appear frequently in geometry diagrams and coordinate problems.

keyFormulas.name: Exterior angle theorem
keyFormulas.latex: \text{exterior angle} = \text{sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles}

keyFormulas.name: Triangle inequality
keyFormulas.latex: \text{Each side} < \text{sum of the other two sides}

workedExamples.problem: In triangle ABC, angle A = 50° and angle B = 70°. What is angle C?
Two similar triangles have a scale factor of 3:5. If the shorter triangle has sides 6, 8, and 10, what is the longest side of the larger triangle?

steps.title: Set up the proportion
steps.content: The scale factor is 5/3. Multiply the corresponding side.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming two triangles are similar just because they look the same in a diagram
commonMistakes.fix: Prove similarity: AA (two pairs of equal angles), SAS (two proportional sides and included angle), or SSS (all three sides proportional).

commonMistakes.mistake: Using the exterior angle as an interior angle in calculations
commonMistakes.fix: An exterior angle is outside the triangle. It equals the sum of the two interior angles not adjacent to it — not the adjacent interior angle.

quickTip: When two parallel lines cross a triangle or create similar triangles in a diagram, proportional sides appear automatically. Look for parallel marks or right-angle marks.
